blogs.title: When HIT Strikes Early: Pre‑operative Heparin Exposure and Post‑Cardiac Surgery Thrombocytopenia
blogs.description: Explore how even a small dose of unfractionated heparin during coronary angiography can precipitate early‑onset heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia after cardiac surgery. We'll review timing thresholds, risk stratification, and practical algorithms for clinicians to recognize and investigate thrombocytopenia that occurs before the classic POD 5‑10 window.

blogs.title: Autoimmune HIT: Heparin‑Independent Platelet Activation and Its Lab Signatures
blogs.description: Delve into the pathophysiology of autoimmune (aHIT) versus classic HIT, focusing on heparin‑independent platelet activation, the role of PF4‑antibody complexes, and the unique serotonin‑release assay patterns—including partial Fc‑receptor blockade resistance as seen in this case. Practical tips for interpreting atypical SRA results will be provided.

blogs.title: Choosing the Right Anticoagulant in Severe HIT: Argatroban vs. Fondaparinux vs. Direct Oral Anticoagulants
blogs.description: Compare the pros and cons of intravenous direct thrombin inhibitors, fondaparinux, and DOACs for managing HIT, especially in patients with bleeding risk, consumptive coagulopathy, and organ dysfunction. The case’s switch from argatroban to fondaparinux will serve as a framework for decision‑making and dosing considerations.

blogs.title: High‑Dose IVIG in Autoimmune HIT: Expectations, Pitfalls, and When It Fails
blogs.description: Review the evidence behind using high‑dose intravenous immunoglobulin for aHIT, mechanisms of action, typical platelet response curves, and reasons for suboptimal response such as ultra‑high antibody titers or Fc‑receptor blockade resistance. The blog will outline monitoring strategies and alternative rescue therapies.

blogs.title: Thrombotic Stroke in the Post‑Operative Cardiothoracic Patient: When HIT Is the Hidden Culprit
blogs.description: Discuss the clinical clues that should raise suspicion for HIT‑related arterial thrombosis in the early postoperative period, including delirium, unexpected platelet falls, and stroke without classic risk factors. Management pathways for acute stroke in the setting of HIT, balancing antiplatelet, anticoagulant, and neuro‑protective measures, will be outlined.

blogs.title: Interpreting Serologic Tests for HIT: From ELISA Positivity to ‘Indeterminate’ SRA and Beyond
blogs.description: Provide a step‑by‑step guide to the diagnostic work‑up of HIT, emphasizing the nuances of ELISA optical density thresholds, serotonin‑release assay patterns, and the significance of heparin‑independent activation. The case’s atypical SRA will be used to illustrate how to avoid mislabeling a true aHIT as a false‑positive or indeterminate result.
